decisions.reason: The low-noise burner is a component shared across the infrared heater range, so keeping it costs little and preserves the option to differentiate the whole line while the 2022 gas-market uncertainty plays out.
The plaque heater had its own page in 2019, which signals commitment, and as part of the core hall-heating portfolio it is cheap to keep while demand under high gas prices remains uncertain.
The luminous radiant heater fits the established infrared business with low holding costs, and the 2019 evidence does not show enough about its value to justify abandoning it yet.
Tube heaters are a staple of industrial hall heating, and the option stays open because the effect of gas-price volatility and the regulatory shift on demand is still unresolved.
The standard plaque heater is a low-cost volume variant with its own page, so it is worth keeping as a cheap option even though it partly overlaps with B.
This second tube heater overlaps with D and could be consolidated, but variant upkeep is cheap and the evidence so far is too thin to justify dropping it now.
